- Use the "外國專業人員工作許可申辦網" (https://ezwp.wda.gov.tw) to apply online for a student work permit. [3]
- The website offers 24‑hour online submission, payment, notification, and inquiry services. [3]
- You only need to provide a copy of your passport; no student ID copy, school consent, transcripts, or special language certificates are required. [3]
- After registering an account, fill out the application form, upload the passport copy, and pay the fee online. [3]

- The maximum fine for a student who works without a work permit is NT$150,000. [4]
- If the employer hires a student without a permit, the employer may be fined up to NT$750,000. [4]
- The employer must follow the Labor Standards Act regarding working hours. [4]
- For more information, visit the Ministry of Labor website (https://www.wda.gov.tw) or call the Labor Ministry hotline 02-8995-6000. [4]

- Use the "行動裝置檢視下載" function to view the electronic work permit on your mobile device. [3]
- Confirm the case information, then print or download the PDF file. [3]

- Use the postal transfer account number 19058848 (勞動部勞動力發展署聘僱許可收費專戶) to pay the application fee. [1]
- Alternatively, you can use an ATM to pay the fee; after obtaining the ATM payment number, pay immediately. [1]

- Foreign students who earn an associate degree or higher in Taiwan can apply to extend their stay in the country for up to two years. [1]
- During the extended stay, graduates can work without obtaining a separate work permit, and family members can also apply to remain in Taiwan. [1]
- The changes simplify the hiring process by eliminating the need for employers to separately apply to the Ministry of Labor for work permits during the extended stay. [1]
- Graduates are not subject to restrictions on the types of professional or technical jobs they can take, employer qualifications or minimum salary thresholds, and can work in any field as long as they comply with labor laws. [1]

- Call 165 for anti-fraud consultation. [4]

- The fine is 10 times the employment insurance premium for the period the employer failed to register the student worker. [1]

- A bachelor's degree takes four years. [3]
- The total number of credits must be at least 128. [3]
- The university adopts the system of academic years and course credits. [3]
- For more details, see the National Central University Study Regulations, Article 13, and the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [3]

- 12 extra graduation credits are required for foreign, Hong Kong, or Macau undergraduates whose graduating grades and schools are equivalent to Taiwan's second year of senior high school. [4]
- Military training and PE do not count toward these 12 credits. [4]
- This requirement is specified in National Central University Study Regulations, Article 48. [4]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [4]

- At least 16 credits each semester in years one to three and at least 9 credits each semester in the fourth academic year. [5]
- If you need to take fewer credits, you must obtain approval from your advisor and department head; otherwise you may be dismissed. [5]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [5]

- International students must take the full-year five-credit course “Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students” (僑生國文) instead of the local requirement. [1]
- Students who take the “Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students” are not required to take the local “Chinese (B): Chinese Writing” course. [1]
- The requirement is 5 credits of Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students. [1]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- 6 credits of Mandarin courses at the Language Center [2]
- File for the Chinese course substitution before you graduate [2]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw [2]

- PE is required for five semesters: Freshman PE I and II plus three PE interest electives. [3]
- The PE courses do not count toward graduation credits. [3]
- You may take an additional 1‑credit PE course after the five semesters, which also does not count toward graduation credits. [3]
- The PE requirement is specified in National Central University Study Regulations, Article 13. [3]

- A master's degree requires at least 24 credits, not counting thesis credits. [4]
- You must also take at least one graduate course of 1 credit or more at NCU; waived courses do not count. [4]

- At least 34 credits, of which at least 18 are doctoral-level, not counting dissertation credits. [5]
- This requirement is stated in National Central University Study Regulations, Article 58. [5]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [5]

- Apply before the add/drop deadline of your first semester [1]
- If approved, you skip both semesters and receive 6 credits that count toward graduation [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 for assistance [1]
- The application process is case‑by‑case for students from English‑speaking countries [1]

- Undergraduates must complete at least 100 service hours on the NCU passport before receiving the degree certificate. [2]
- You can check your hours on the Service Learning Website or in the Graduation System. [2]
- If you have questions, contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs (學務處服務學習發展中心). [2]
- The Service Learning Website is https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/. [2]

- Service learning is not listed as a graduation condition for master's and doctoral students. [4]
- The graduation conditions for master's and doctoral students are completing all required courses and credits, passing the degree examination, and receiving satisfactory conduct grades each semester. [4]
- Individual departments may set additional requirements. [4]
- Contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs (學務處服務學習發展中心) at https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/ for more information. [4]

- The service-learning course is a zero-credit required course that must be taken in two semesters. [5]
- The two course numbers of the service-learning courses taken by a student shall not be identical. [5]
- The course numbers must be different. [5]
- Contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs at https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/. [5]
